correctness.rationale: The Dirichlet(1,1,1) circular spacings imply constant half-angle density 8/pi^2 on a simplex of area pi^2/8. The standard triangle identity gives R=4 prod sin(half-angle). A Jacobian-one change to the half-angle difference yields exactly the stated arccosine survival integral with correctly solved threshold roots. Near each simplex vertex the small-radius sublevel region has area (t/4) log(1/t) to leading order, and the three edges away from vertices are lower order; the resulting constant is 6/pi^2. At the unique equilateral maximum, expansion R=1/2-2(u^2+uv+v^2)+O(norm^3) yields ellipse area pi epsilon/sqrt(3), hence 8/(pi sqrt(3)). Boundary cases, normalization, and known independent first two moments were checked. The embedded checker directly compares Cartesian inradii, CDF quadrature, and asymptotic coefficient trends; it is supplementary, not a proof.

value.rationale: The inradius is a canonical measure of thickness/quality for a triangle with fixed circumcircle. A complete probability law for the most elementary random inscribed triangle measures an intrinsic size statistic not fixed by area, perimeter, angle marginals, or the previously known two moments. The logarithmic rarity of nearly degenerate incircles and linear rarity of nearly optimal incircles represent two distinct and geometrically explained tail mechanisms; the constants allow exact benchmark probabilities and asymptotic comparisons. The exact one-dimensional integral and endpoint classification are natural finite-dimensional geometric-probability outputs, not arbitrary parameter slices.
